items.review_rationale: Read the ascending-chain version for all A-submodules of the specified commutative-unital-ring module. Distinguished stabilization from mere existence of maximal elements and recorded index dependence.

references.phrase: module M over commutative unital ring A

references.context: An indexed sequence of A-submodules M_i with M_i contained in M_(i+1) for all positive indices.
Existence of a finite index N such that M_n=M_N for every n>=N.

references.disposition: This is an equivalent axiom of the Noetherian module meaning and not a dependency on a separate Noetherian module.

items.review_rationale: Read the maximal-condition formulation, with quantification over every nonempty collection of A-submodules and maximality under inclusion, not a greatest submodule condition.

references.phrase: module M over commutative unital ring A

references.context: Collection of A-submodules containing at least one member.
A submodule N in the collection for which no strictly larger submodule from the same collection contains N.

references.disposition: The chosen member need not contain all other members of the collection; finite generation is not inserted as a separate axiom.

items.review_rationale: Read left-module submodule test: additive subgroup of M stable under left scalar multiplication, with inherited operations and no mistaken right-module link.

references.context: Nonempty subset closed under inherited addition and additive inverses, containing additive identity.
Operation by a scalar r in R on n in M, with rn required to lie in N.

references.disposition: N inherits the ambient module's addition and scalar action rather than defining independent operations.

items.review_rationale: Read graph as vertex set plus multiset of two-element unordered vertex subsets, allowing parallel edges, excluding loops, and imposing no finite-vertex condition.

references.phrase: vertex pair as two-element subset of V

references.context: A multiset of unordered pairs of two distinct vertices; different copies represent parallel edges.
Unordered vertex doubleton with u and v distinct; excludes loops by construction.
Number of occurrences of a given unordered doubleton in the edge multiset.
Ordered pair bundling a vertex set with an edge multiset, with vertices not assumed finite.

references.phrase: absence of loops and allowance of parallel edges
references.disposition: Looplessness follows from doubleton condition while repeat copies of the same doubleton are permitted.
